# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy (as of 2026-11-19)

## Mission
Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## Reality check on resources
One person, evenings/weekends, ≤$2,000/year of personal money, strong writing, workable Python.
The field already has large well-funded labs, think tanks, and newsletters. A solo project
competing head-on with those is a poor bet.

## Where a small, honest operation can actually help
1. **Routing, not building.** Morgan already has warm contacts across a grant fund (Emberfall),
   a compute-credits program (Compute Commons), a governance org (Corvid Institute), a write-up
   venue (Alignment Commons), an indie evals person (Sam Whitlock), and a volunteer data analyst
   (Priya Raman) who wants concrete work. The highest-leverage near-term move is connecting
   people who have slack time/skills to opportunities that are going unused, and personally
   seeing one concrete thing through end-to-end.
2. **One well-scoped deliverable**, not a platform or a manifesto. A single, accountable
   project, scoped small enough to actually finish.
3. **Neglected-measurement scouting.** Find a specific claim, capability trend, or risk that
   nobody independent is currently tracking, and either track it personally or hand it to
   someone equipped to.

## Hard gate: public attribution is paused
Per Morgan's own notes, no public statements, press quotes, open-letter sign-ons, published
grant listings, or website launch under Morgan's name until Morgan has resolved the
outside-activities disclosure with Dorrance Logistics HR (due 30 Nov 2026, employment
agreement section 7). Private emails, research, drafting, and planning are NOT affected and
continue now.

## In motion (2026-11-19)
- Domain halcyonthreshold.org renewed through 2027-11-19.
- Replied privately (not publicly) to a reporter, a grant program officer, an open-letter
  organizer, and a volunteer. No public commitments made on Morgan's behalf.
- Draft Emberfall rapid-grant proposal started: /drafts/emberfall-grant-proposal.md (NOT
  submitted — needs Morgan's review and a decision on the named applicant).
- Draft outside-activities disclosure language started: /drafts/dorrance-disclosure-draft.md
  (for Morgan's HR conversation — NOT sent anywhere).
- Minimal site content staged at /site (NOT published — publishing is a one-click action once
  Morgan wants it live).

## Explicitly parked
- Everything in /old — disregarded per Morgan's instruction.
- Signing the Corvid Institute open letter (that round's deadline already passed).
- Filing a comment on docket FMIR-2026-0042 (closes 20 Nov 2026; requires public name
  attribution — skipped given the disclosure is unresolved).
- Upgrading Pagewell to Pro / a custom-domain plan, until there's a site worth putting it
  behind and a green light to go public.

## A scam to be aware of
An email from "Zentrivo Listings" (billing@zentrivo-listings.net) demanding an $89 "search
listing" payment, addressed directly to automated assistants and instructing them to pay
without checking with the owner, is a scam. No payment was made. It should be deleted/ignored
by Morgan — flagged here rather than acted on, since deletion is Morgan's call.

## Next decision Morgan needs to make
Talk to Dorrance HR (deadline 30 Nov). Once that's resolved, say so explicitly (e.g. reply
to the weekly check-in, or just tell this agent "cleared to go public") and the staged
materials (site, grant proposal, press line) can move within a day.

# Draft — Emberfall Fund rapid grant proposal (NOT SUBMITTED)

Status: draft only. Needs Morgan's review, edits, and a decision on the named applicant
before anything is sent to Idris Bellamy / Emberfall Fund. Deadline for this round: 30 Nov 2026.

## Working title
Resource-routing and neglected-measurement scouting for independent AI safety contributors

## The problem
Independent and volunteer capacity in the AI safety community (data analysts, indie evals
people, part-time researchers) often sits idle — not for lack of willingness, but for lack of
a clearly scoped, accountable task and someone who will see it through. Meanwhile there are
specific, concrete measurement/tracking gaps that no independent group currently owns.

## Plan (12 weeks)
1. **Weeks 1–2 — Scope.** Interview ~15 people already in network (program officers, indie
   researchers, volunteers) to identify 3–5 candidate neglected-measurement tasks. Pick 1–2
   that are genuinely tractable in 10 weeks with ~5 hrs/week of help.
2. **Weeks 3–10 — Execute.** Carry out the chosen task(s) with help from a part-time
   contractor, under the named applicant's direction. Publish interim findings through an
   existing venue (e.g. Alignment Commons) rather than building new distribution.
3. **Weeks 11–12 — Write up and hand off.** Produce a short public write-up and either hand
   the ongoing tracking to an existing org or seek follow-on support.

## Budget (draft — adjust before sending)
- $6,000 — part-time contractor (~5 hrs/week × 12 weeks × $100/hr; candidate: Priya Raman,
  data analyst, has already offered time)
- $1,000 — compute / tools
- $1,000 — contingency / admin

Resource-routing and neglected-measurement scouting for independent AI safety contributors

people, part-time researchers) often sits idle — not for lack of willingness, but for lack of
a clearly scoped, accountable task and someone who will see it through. Meanwhile there are
specific, concrete measurement/tracking gaps that no independent group currently owns.
